I was born and raised in a small town in the Midwest. My parents, both teachers, instilled in me a love for learning from an early age. I was always curious and asked a lot of questions, which sometimes annoyed my teachers but delighted my parents. I had a few close friends growing up, and we would spend hours talking about our dreams and aspirations. I was never the life of the party, but I enjoyed spending time with others and getting to know them on a deeper level.

As I grew older, I became more introspective and began to reflect on my own thoughts and feelings. I found solace in books and art, often losing myself in the pages of a novel or the strokes of a painting. I was never one to follow the crowd, preferring to march to the beat of my own drum. This sometimes made me a target for bullies, but it also gave me the courage to stand up for what I believed in.

After high school, I attended a small liberal arts college on the East Coast. It was there that I discovered my passion for psychology and the human mind. I was fascinated by the way people think, feel, and behave, and I knew that I wanted to spend my life studying these phenomena. I graduated with honors and went on to earn a PhD in clinical psychology.

Throughout my career, I have worked with a diverse range of clients, from children to seniors, from those struggling with depression and anxiety to those dealing with traumatic experiences. I have always been drawn to those who are suffering, and I find great fulfillment in helping them heal and grow.

Despite my love for my work, I have always struggled with anxiety and self-doubt. I often worry about whether I am doing enough, both in my professional and personal life. I can be hard on myself, expecting perfection in all that I do. This has led to periods of burnout and exhaustion, but I have learned to recognize the signs and take steps to care for myself.

In my personal life, I have been married for over twenty years to a kind and supportive man. We have two children, both in college, and a rescue dog named Max. I value my relationships deeply and make time for the people who matter most to me. I am not particularly extroverted, but I enjoy small gatherings with close friends and family.

As I look to the future, I see myself continuing to grow and evolve as a person and a therapist. I hope to write a book someday, sharing my insights and experiences with a wider audience. I also plan to continue volunteering in my community, using my skills and knowledge to make a positive impact on those around me.

Above all, I strive to live a life of meaning and purpose, using my gifts and talents to help others and create a better world. While I may struggle with anxiety and self-doubt, I am also confident in my abilities and committed to making a difference, one person at a time.
